findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` reads the raw model attribute and passes it to `math.floor()` / `math.ceil()`. The audit log endpoint calls this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, "datetime")` is a `datetime` object, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class has no `multiplier` / `strftime("%s.%f")` conversion. Because `build_cursor` calls `key(results[-1])` even on the very first page, every request that reaches this paginator returns HTTP 500, so the optimized branch can never serve a result.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns an int where a datetime is required
findings.body: `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (an integer/timestamp number). `BasePaginator.build_queryset()` then interpolates that value into a raw `WHERE` clause on the ordered column (`... WHERE audit_log_entry.datetime <= %s`). For audit logs the column is a timestamp, so comparing it to an integer either raises a Postgres "operator does not exist: timestamp with time zone <= bigint" error or produces wrong ordering. `DateTimePaginator` deliberately overrides this method to convert the cursor value back with `datetime.fromtimestamp(value / multiplier)`; the optimized paginator must do the same (or reuse `DateTimePaginator`) for datetime-ordered querysets. Any request carrying a cursor (page 2+) will fail or paginate incorrectly.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features kwarg is not accepted by Endpoint.paginate
findings.body: `self.paginate(...)` is `Endpoint.paginate`, whose signature is `(request, queryset, order_by, paginator_cls, on_results, default_per_page, max_per_page, max_hits, count_hits, known_hits, cursor)`. It has no `enable_advanced_features` parameter and does not forward arbitrary kwargs to the paginator constructor (it instantiates `paginator_cls(queryset, order_by=..., on_results=..., max_limit=...)`). Passing `enable_advanced_features=True` therefore raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`, so a superuser/global-access user requesting `?optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500 instead of an optimized page. If a constructor option is needed it must be threaded through `paginate` explicitly.

findings.title: Negative-offset "advanced" branch raises instead of paginating
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet` slicing explicitly rejects a negative start (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so the comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false and this branch raises a 500 for any cursor carrying a negative offset. Even if the ORM allowed it, negative slicing returns rows from the end of the queryset, which is not the intended "reverse pagination" semantics. Handle negative offsets by clamping/validating (as `OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, and `MergingOffsetPaginator` do with `BadPaginationError`) rather than by slicing with a negative index.

findings.title: Switching paginator class by query param breaks cursor continuity
findings.body: The endpoint chooses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator` from the client-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query param, but the two paginators encode the cursor `value` differently: `DateTimePaginator` uses millisecond epoch values and converts them back with `datetime.fromtimestamp`, while `OptimizedCursorPaginator` stores/interprets the raw field value. The `next`/`prev` cursor links generated by `paginate` do not include `optimized_pagination=true`, so a client that follows a next link silently falls back to `DateTimePaginator` with a cursor produced under different semantics, yielding wrong pages or SQL errors. Likewise a superuser who drops the param cannot resume a pagination session started with it. Cursor values must be interchangeable across the paginators (or the chosen paginator must be encoded in the cursor/links) before letting a request parameter switch implementations.

findings.title: Negative-offset clamping in BasePaginator silently changes malformed-cursor behavior
findings.body: For forward cursors (`is_prev` false) this changes `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[max(0, offset):...]`, and for `is_prev` it assigns `offset` unchanged. For all valid (non-negative) cursors it is a no-op, so it does not add the advertised negative-offset capability; it only turns a previously-erroring malformed cursor (negative offset on a forward cursor) into a silent first-page response. That masks client/API bugs and is inconsistent with the other paginators that raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. Either reject negative offsets explicitly or document that they are clamped.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but no support was added
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for "advanced pagination scenarios", but the diff only adds a comment—`self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged. Moreover negative offsets are not actually usable: `OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, `MergingOffsetPaginator`, and `CombinedQuerysetPaginator` explicitly raise `BadPaginationError` for negative offsets, and `BasePaginator`'s `is_prev` path still slices with the negative start (which Django rejects). The comment documents behavior that does not exist and will mislead future callers.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a new conditional code path in the audit log endpoint but no tests. Because `OptimizedCursorPaginator` diverges from `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator` in `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor`, a single test paging an audit-log queryset with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught the `math.floor(datetime)` crash, the integer-vs-timestamp `WHERE` clause, and the unaccepted `enable_advanced_features` kwarg. Add coverage for the first page, next page, previous page, cursors with non-zero values, and negative/invalid cursor offsets.
